Review: So I've been a pretty big fan of Amazon stuff for sometime. I use Amazon Basics stuff whenever I can. I also rarely leave reviews.But this thing was a big enough disappointment and continues to be a frustration that I figured people need to know some stuff.First off, as an Alexa device, it's fine. Plays music, does the 4 other things Alexa is able to do (different rant).But one of the main reasons I got this thing wasn't for Alexa or as just a music player, I wanted to make a 2-studio-1-subwoofer home theater.Well it really sucks at that so far. Connecting using the Alexa app is fairly simple, but it just refuses to be a reliable home theater system. It constantly drops sound, or has intermittent sound loss. Happens randomly. Sometimes I'll just turn on the TV and only the sub will be working. So I'll have to recreate the entire home theater system. It's also really picky about what it will and won't work with.Also it refuses to connect via wired Ethernet like its fire TV brethren. And if the fire TV you want to make the home theater with isn't on the same SSID (as in, if my fire TV is connected via wired Ethernet and the studio\sub aren't) then it also makes problems.As for sound quality, it's good not great. It doesn't quite fill a large, open floor plan family room. If you're looking for a better sound quality home theater than a comparably priced sound bar\sub combo will probably beat whatever studio\sub combo (dollar to dollar). I know going from my 6 year old LG soundbar\sub to the studios\sub did not improve overall sound quality to any noticeable amount. But I also got it for home automation reasons so I was ok with that.I think if you want this for just a much better version of the echo plus that plays music then you'll be happy, but hold off for at least another 6-12 months if you're looking for a home theater upgrade.

Review: I bought these hoping to replace an ancient JBL wired computer speaker set. In general, I love Bose speakers—I have one set of 301s over 40 years old that are still kicking after a refoam, as well as near and far-range studio monitors and a home theater setup. So I am comparing Revolve to the ancient computer speakers here.I found the 360 sound in the Revolve Series II lacking, to the point of a marketing gimmick. With just one speaker, I felt off-balance, so I bought a second speaker. Stereo mode sounds okay, deep base, kind of muddy with little separation. Unfortunately, there is no way to EQ them in the Bose App, which would be a marked improvement. If you are playing music from an iPhone you can select different EQ settings—of which I found "Flat" to be the best option for most tracks.They're okay for computer speakers and are adequate for near-range listening of fewer than ten feet, but not full enough to use one speaker per area in party mode. In addition, they sound harsh to my ears at higher volumes. However, the small footprint and portability are an advantage. The design is excellent, and the profile is discreet.Would I repurchase them? Due to the range of decent speakers at a lower price point in this category, probably not. However, combined with the JBL speakers, the Bose Revolve II speakers create a more immersive sound for my home office setup without taking up much desk space.

Review: I bought a 1st gen shortly after it came out. I have use it daily since it arrived. The sound quality was always enough that I could hear the music but couldn't really pick up a while lot of detail and the low end frequency was really missing. Also, it didn't blend in with the living room decor, so it seemed to stick out a bit.The 2nd gen. has made big improvements to both. The Echo delivers cleaner, fuller sound while at the same time bringing enough low end to get really good all-around sound from a single speaker. The shorter wider profile along with the fabric cover make it fit in about anywhere in the living room. Microphone sensitivity and range is about the same as the original. The only negative thing I could say about it is I wish it still had the ring for volume adjustment. It made it easier to turn down after one of the kids had been listening to their music at near full volume or adjusting to just the right level for listening to music when company is over. Not that you can't do it by voice command, or the buttons on top of the new version, just a personal preference.Overall, I love it. Between cooking instructions, drink ideas, reminders, timers, linked calendars, smart lights (a must have,) alarms, news (even local), weather, not to mention my Spotify (and more I don't feel like typing out), I am certainly getting my money's worth.

It set up very easily and was connected to my account without problem.  Within less than a week, every time I asked "Alexa" to perform a task (eg. play music, play NPR), she would start the task briefly and then freeze with a loud annoying buzz and would fail to respond again, until 1) she seemed to reset herself, or 2) I unplugged her and plugged her back in.  I phoned and spoke with tech support for Alexa devices (outsourced to the Philippines) with whom I spent about an hour on the phone, while he coached me through various attempts to fix, including resetting the device.  None of this worked.  I asked for an exchange, and when I *specifically asked* to make sure I'd be getting a brand new device, he said yes of course I would get a new device.  Well, he LIED.  Amazon tech support LIED.  What I ended up getting in return was "Echo Studio - High-fidelity smart speaker with 3D audio and Alexa - R".  The "- R" means REFURBISHED!  I bought a BRAND NEW device, had it for less than 1 week, was lied to about the replacement being new, and ended up with a REFURBISHED device.  There is terrible customer support!  Why not just return the defective device for a refund and re-buy a brand new one?  Because when I bought it on November 22, it was a special deal for a cheaper price, bundled with two "free" Phillips Hue bulbs.  It's back up to full price now.  That said, see for yourself in my video (taken just today before I return the defective unit to Amazon).  I hope Amazon takes this review seriously: defective device, time wasted with subpar customer support, and a refurbished device for exchange is not what anyone should come to expect from Amazon.

Review: The first wave of units shipped had an equalizer problem and sounded awful!  I preordered my walnut woodgrain Echo and it arrived a couple days after the non-woodgrain Echos.  While reading the reviews for the two days before mine arrived I was nervous!  It seemed like most people hated this new 2nd generation Echo.  Mine finally arrived and it too sounded terrible!  After a few hours of not using it the update downloaded and all the sudden it sounded great!  The speaker has broken in and it actually has BASS!  I waited awhile to leave my review to make sure I really liked this Echo.  I went to a big box store and listened to some other bluetooth speakers and this Echo blows all of them away (even two Bose speakers that I tried but maybe the floor models were abused).  The walnut grain is really nice and looks rich.  It goes with my room decor really well.  One of my most used features on the Echo is the nature sounds for sleeping.  There are some great rain sounds that you can put on loop while you sleep!  I also hook up the Echo to my tablet so the sound comes out of the Echo instead of the tablets dinky speakers.  Watching youtube with the Echo as my speaker has been great!  I will be buying another one eventually.  I have two Echo dots also.  One of the dots is hooked up to Klipsch speakers on a stereo system and the sound is obviously much better but for the size of this Echo you really can't beat the sound.  Bottome line: don't let the bad reviews sway you away from this thing.  Amazon's return policy is the best so at least give it a try and see what you think.  I'm super picky about everything and I couldn't be happier with this device.

Review: "Set up in minutes"?? Not really. There are no actual detailed instructions included. I tried scanning the QR code that was provided in the little pamphlet, and that was not helpful. This ended up being extremely frustrating to set up. I could take a wild guess that I was supposed put the lithium batteries in the back of the camera. I would not have known that the little QR code inside the camera where the batteries go was something that I had to scan to set up the camera. Anyway, without going into detail, if Amazon provided some simple, basic instructions with photos that show step by step, it would save the customer a ton of fumbling around. Then it might have been an easy set up. I had to call for support, and by the time I got a support person on the phone I was pretty irritated. The reason I decided to buy this camera is the "two-year battery life." Note: these are not rechargeable batteries. We'll see how long the batteries last. Prior to this, I got a Eufy Solocam, also wireless (and much, much easier to set up), and it had rechargeable batteries advertised to last 4 months, but they lasted 4 weeks. A feature that is missing with the Blink camera, that I liked on the Eufy camera, is the AI feature to recognize humans. Without the AI feature, the Blink is recording non-human motion, such as animals and vehicles.Update: The description advertises customized zones for motion detection. The camera takes a photo what it sees, and in motion settings, you gray out areas that you do not want the camera to detect motion. It does NOT work. I tried resetting it several times, and the camera recorded and sent me an alert of motion detected that was squarely in the grayed out area. Without this feature actually working, and without the AI feature to detect humans, the camera is recording every motion in the entire viewable area, ignoring the areas that I grayed out. I am returning this camera.

Review: This device is awesome when it works - which is less than 50% of the time.  The connectivity with my existing sonos network is wonky, inconsistent, and unreliable.  Sonos Move is constantly dropping off of the network.  Half the time I cannot see the Sonos Move in the sonos app running on any of my devices (ipads, iphones, android tablets, etc.).  This problem is even more prevalent when removing it from the dock for portable use (the entire value proposition of Move is its portability).  NO, it is not my wifi network - everything else on my wifi network is working fine (incl. my other sonos devices) and I am using a very new mesh router (Netgear Nighthawk).  Sonos's help/support has been quite limited and their recommended  solution is to perform a factory reset to resolve the connection issue.  I have owned the Sonos Move for 6 months and have had to perform over a dozen factory resets.  No firmware updates have been issued to resolve this problem (I am not the only one-check the user/help community on Sonos.com - it is filled with similar experiences).  Connectivity with Apple AirPlay and even simple Bluetooth is nearly as unreliable and inconsistent.  Very frustrating to work with this device and so unlike all of the other Sonos products I have been using for about 5 years (Sonos One, Connect, etc.).  Each time I use it, I have to cross my fingers and hope it works.  I am reluctant to purchase anything else from Sonos again, until they make things right with Move.  I have to wonder if the product launch was expedited or hurried along despite these technical shortcomings.  Sonos is now touting Roam and perhaps that is the diversion from the failure that is Move.  My money spent on Move is essentially a dead-weight loss.  I'd be just as well served with a 1980s boombox.

Review: After using the Echo for about a month, I can say it is at best "entertaining" at trying to make it understand what you want.  It's search for trivia is lacking.  If you expect results like you would get with a google search, you will be very disappointed.A lot of times my wife and I are watching TV and we ask Alexa about an actor or actress, and many times we come up short and resort to google on our tablet.Adding skills can add to the functionality, but many of the skills are more for marketing purposes rather than providing useful functionality to you.  There is a "DeWalt Tools" skill that will let you ask:  "Alexa, ask DeWalt Tools what is your history"...  I'd like to meet any person who would find this skill useful... just so I could ask "WHY?  Why would you enable such a useless skill?"I can see Alexa being much more useful if you have smart devices in your home, such as a connected thermostat, roomba, garage door opener, etc.  as asking Alexa to change the thermostat setting, or asking if the garage door is open, would be very useful.Using Alexa to add events to my google calendar is also not quite ready for prime-time.  You would think this would be relatively easy, however, how Alexa and Google handle timezones creates a problem.  (Alexa does not send timezone information with the request, so google assumes the time is GMT when storing the event, however, since google has my timezone set as PST - it converts the GMT time to PST when displaying it.)  Personally - IMO Google has this correct, and Alexa should send my timezone with the request to create the event.  After all, she knows my timezone.On the brighter side - Alexa does have an opinion - albeit clinical - to the question "Alexa - does size really matter?"

The quality of the camera was good, but the spotlight was very annoying (depending on the amount of light in your house, it can be more than a tad overzealous). Review: The Alexa Hardware (especially the 2nd and 3rd Gen devices) are amazing things.  Whether a Dot or Echo or Plus, the Microphone Array works as expected from even a room away. Ask her to use a PIN to complete the Pairing process, and she CAN'T even though she can well understand your instructions and your PIN Value.  Ask her to play music from your PC DLNA or iTunes or NAS located on the same Home Network, and she can't unless you expose those resources to the Internet for connectivity through Amazon's AWS Cloud.  And don't expect Alexa to understand and navigate all of the features of your Amazon Account - Amazon Household is only supported in pieces; she can't handle an Audible Account unless it has an Amazon Account Login; and when you want to play Your Music she will often default to iHeartRadio or try to push an Amazon Music Unlimited Account.  But, Alexa is well versed in Selling you ALL of the Products and Programs and Offerings - that IS her JOB, after all.

Review: CON:  Fitbit’s algorithm for calculating heart rate needs work.  Perhaps their engineers did not test the watch on a range of ages and body types.  I have tried their suggestions like wearing the watch higher on the wrist, or tighter, or in a different position on the wrist (like inside), but none of these made any difference with the heart rate inaccuracy.  In short, my watch says I am exercising more strenuously than I actually am!EXAMPLE:  My Fitbit gives heart rates in the 140-160 range (near my maximum) while jogging.  I took my pulse manually and the actual rate was only around 110-120.I tested the Fitbit against two pulse oximeters (see photos).  Both pulse oximeters agreed on the heart rate, while the Fitbit was consistently far too high until the rate got closer to 100 or below it.  Then, the Fitbit often matched the pulse oximeters (or nearly so).So, if you are using your Fitbit to monitor heart rate with exercise that keeps your heart rate nearer 100 or below, it will be more accurate than an exercise that tends to keep your heart rate higher, like jogging or running.PROS:  I have liked the sleep monitor function and the health metrics, especially the heart rate variability, which is interesting to track.WISHES:  I wish more could be done via the computer rather than the cell.  Would like greater accessibility to the raw data.  Would appreciate being able to track health metrics for more than a week.

To my knowledge the Studio speakers do NOT sync with another Studio to produce a true one-room directional stereo sound field.  I didn't really want that (if I did I'd get the Sonus).  My unit sits on the kitchen breakfast bar, a bit away from one wall, and it sounds great.  I've not tried it on the floor or a bookshelf - just remember that the speaker self-adjusts to different locations so it will sound a bit different as you move it around - I recall there are instructions on this aspect.  For now, for the price, I think the upgrade is great, cost effective, meets my needs for enhanced audio.  I actually like the squatty charcoal look! Bravo Amazon! Keep it up. Review: I've had similar fitness/wellness tracking devices before and have to admit once the initial intrigue wore off, I stopped using them.  However, working with a medical professional, I was highly recommended to get back on this technology bandwagon and decided to purchase this particular option.  I'm an IT professional and work with data and computing constantly.  That said, I prefer to turn-off technology in the rest of my life, so to me, "less is more" really fits my personal preferences and behavior with using personal technology like this.  I purchased this because of all my options it seemed the best value for the money (and cheapest for what I was asked to purchase by my medical professional) and had the fewest "features."  Even with that, it frankly has more "features" than I need - sleep tracking? - no thanks, got that covered elsewhere - PAI? - I don't have a clue, nor do I care, what that means - Heart Rate and SpO2? - OK, but again, not a burning concern and something I have covered elsewhere if needed.  Really, just need a pedometer.  For that, this seems fine to me and does seem accurate versus other products I've used in the past.  As for the necessary interface/bluetooth with a mobile phone, from my perspective, just an added layer of technology that I personally could do without - why can't the device just provide me, self-contained, that data I'm looking for?  But, I will say that it was not hard to setup that interface with my mobile phone, so I guess that's o.k.  I will say the delivered options for basic display of time/date/steps/battery life were welcome and glad I had a choice.  At least this makes this more useful as a potential watch substitute on my wrist versus other versions of this type of technology I've used in the past.  I'm also good with the battery life and ease in re-charging.

Review: My wife got an Inspire 2 several weeks ago. I decided to go for the Charge 5 because of its larger face, color, and promise of "up to 7 days" battery life. I got nothing close to that. Turns out this is an issue you can find in the Fitbit community forum, a resource open to all registered users. As others who experienced the same problem reported, I had turned off GPS, set notification vibrations to normal, and disabled "always on display." I also reset the device. None of it helped. Didn't get much past 24 hours before receiving a low battery warning via email. By contrast, a full charge on my wife's Inspire 2 easily lasts a week. Yes it has fewer features and is harder to read with its black and white smaller face, particularly in direct sunlight. But it connects to the same app and comes with a year's free premium trial instead of only 6 months. (Dumb marketing thinking on Fitbit's part, IMO).  So I'm "trading down" to my wife's model. I also found the Charge 5's menu counterintuitive and clunky in some areas. If you watch Charge 5 YouTube vids you'll find that even relatively experienced users struggle at times to get the device to behave as you'd expect. Bottom line: I'd have kept the Charge 5 if not for its poor battery life.

I haven't taken the speaker completely apart so I haven't checked the voice coil, but the magnet is also much heavier. The surround (annulus) seems more pliant.All this results in better sound.This model has two dome tweeters for slightly better mids and highs and better directionality in both mono and especially stereo modes.Of course it isn't a replacement for a home stereo, and it is was never meant to be. Review: Easy to setup and install. The Ring company includes all the necessary tools (minus the power drill) to mount the device and get you up and running within an hour. You just have to decide beforehand where to mount the device. The instructions do recommend you charge the battery for a longer period but if you need immediate surveillance the battery is low but it is good to go. My take away point, I like the fact that I don’t have to wire a power cable to the device, it has a rechargeable. Review: I received my Charge 5 as a Christmas gift the end of 2021 and it's now the summer of 2022.  At first I was thrilled with it.  It was stacked with options, tracked the things I was most interested in, seemed quite accurate and came at a good price point.  Unfortunately, after only a few months of using it, however, it started losing battery life very quickly... like it would go from 80% charged to dead in a few hours... not the days they tout.  I contacted support, who told me it was a known issue and encouraged me to do a few things like disabling GPS, display "always on" and tracking SpO2 (all reasons I bought the tracker in the first place, but okay).  I also found that by resetting the device every couple of days helped.  Between those two things it seemed to be working okay.While out for a jog the other day, however, a red X showed up on the screen, soon after it powered down and I haven’t been able to get it to turn on since.  I tried charging it, but that seems to do nothing.  From a quick Google search I found a recommendation to reset the tracker by pressing the button on the charging cable three times... nothing.  I also cleaned the charging pins and tried using different bricks for charging… again nothing has helped.  Sadly, I think it might be dead for good.If I had it for a year or more, I would be much more understanding.  Granted, I do train pretty hard (CrossFit 5-6 times a week) and I definitely put my gear to the test... but 6 months?!  Come on... this tracker should have lasted longer than that.  Now I guess I'm on the hunt for something more reliable and durable... but probably more expensive.

That would be great if actually did, but just because a song has lyrics like sweet dreams, it doesn't mean that song will lull an 18 year old kid to sleep, or keep them asleep when they are on the verge of nodding out, especially if there are freaking TRUMPETS blaring in the chorus! It's also not nice to lock us into shuffle when you want to set a mood to go to sleep, which is what I do on my Lullabies playlist. I purposely never shuffle it so that the more stimulating music is at the beginning not in the middle or the end! Nice move Amazon. You just lost a sell.

Please try again.  If issue persists, please contact customer support for further assistance."  I'm fairly sure I configured it correctly because it would work about 50% of the time, but it was too frustrating to only have it work half the time as sometimes you might have to restart it 2-5 times in a row.I read the FAQs for the camera and did everything they suggested there.  I also contacted TP-Link support who had me reboot my router but that did not fix the problem.Conclusion:  Good image quality camera and seems to work well with it's own app.  But at least at this time it doesn't seem to work well with the Google devices for displaying the camera (for me anyway).  Perhaps a future update of their software might fix this, but for right now it didn't work reliably for me, bad enough that sadly I'm returning it.In addition with the Google displays it will only view the camera for 10 minutes before stopping.  Apparently with the App (if it's on the same WiFi) you can have continuous viewing, but with the Google displays it will only view for 10 minutes before stopping.

Recently I purchased a Sono's Move ($400) and this one item sounds much better than the three amazon devices combined which cost $530 and it is substantially more reliable.  Unfortunately, I am stuck with $1,060 of Amazon devices that are unreliable, and I just carry the Sono's Move around from room to room versus hoping the Echo studio pairs will work.  If you are looking for a budget standalone item this may be a good purchase, but if you are looking for a reliable speaker configuration this is not the correct choice.  Again, I love amazon and will continue to try all of their new products because I think overall, they are spectacular but this product when configured in a speaker pair is unreliable and of subpar quality for the cost.

Average pace, for instance, no longer reflects how fast you ran, but rather correlates with how long you spent at the end standing still while the timer ticks up and you are JUST TRYING TO GET IT TO STOP.Pictured: a run I just went on. You'll see very clearly the moment I stopped running. That whole drop off was me drying the fitbit, washing my hands, and just pressing those side sensors OVER AND OVER trying to get it to respond. This happens EVERY run.All this really needs is to replace the sensors with actual buttons or else to have a way to end the exercise from the touch screen on the watches face, which is way more responsive.

Review: My Echo Dot works pretty much the way I expected it to.  But, I did not anticipate the wonky performance of Alexa compatible devices.  I use 4 Kasa Smart switches for 4 lamps throughout my house.  The switches work reliably as long as I use the Kasa app.  But, the Alexa interface with the Kasa app is completely unreliable.  I must reset the connection with Alexa multiple times each day.  Inevitably,  when I want to turn on a lamp.  It doesn't work & I must invoke the Alexa app to "Discover Devices" again.  It's easier just to turn on the lamp normally.  It's NOT the switches.  It's the connection between the Kasa app & the Alexa system!UPDATE: Because of my unfavorable review of Alexa systems, an Echo Dot rep contacted me. (Note: the rep was only qualified on my 2 Echo Dots. I also have an Alexa Fire TV Cube that the Echo Dot rep could not discuss. A different Alexa customer service office handles the Fire TV Cube. Very inconvenient!) After more than 2 hours on the phone & more iterations of diagnostic steps than I can remember, we determined that the Kasa TP-Link software needed to be updated & all Alexa & Kasa devices, including my wireless router, needed to be rebooted by disconnecting power & restarting them. The rep followed a script initially, but soon exhausted that & resorted to basically "trial & error". The good news is that, after a week of flaky Alexa performance, I have been able to use Alexa to control my Kasa switches for 24 hours without interruption. Wooo hooo! I still give Alexa two stars for performance, but I give the Echo Dot rep 10 out of 5 stars for perseverance!

Review: It took a large investment of time and money to set these up.  Then I realized they don’t do me much good because of several design flaws.Since they’re designed to stay charged years off of a couple of batteries, they weren't designed to be capturing or viewing much at all.  However I need them to at times.  I unload trucks at the back of store I own and want to be able to monitor the front of the store from my phone, so know if customers enter and need help.  The app makes you press a button to continue every 30 seconds while monitoring, or else auto disconnects (in which case you’re taking the time to wait for the app to reconnect to a camera again, before it auto disconnects again soon later).I realize that leaving a camera active eats the battery, but I’d rather have the option to not-auto-disconnect and put new batteries in every month, than for this power-saving feature to make this camera and app nearly worthless. (At least let me set up an auto-off time.  2 minutes would be way less annoying than 30 seconds).Instead, this camera/app combo strives to be good at monitoring “while armed”, recording for a few seconds and sending you a notification.  This might be useful if you could set up a schedule, or else start monitoring when leaving the hub area.  As far as I can figure out, I have to manually arm the cameras, which has happened one time over the couple of weeks I’ve used it.Everything else seems as good as expected from a compact, wifi-reliant, cutting-edge security system.

Review: We were looking for indoor cameras to be able to check on our dog when we were away. Then we noticed that some animal had been digging in our vegetable garden and wanted to set up an outdoor camera to try to figure out what it was. Amazon had an early Prime day sale on these so we got this Blink Outdoor for the garden, and a Blink indoor and Blink Mini for checking on the dog.One of the things we liked about these was that we don't have to have a subscription to be able to check on our videos, although without the subscription the functionality is limited. Still, it's fine for our needs. However, we noticed that the IR view outdoors is terrible. The images are either very washed out, so as not to be able to see any detail, or too dark to be useful. The sound on the videos is attrocious. It's muffled and distorted.The small size is great and the long battery life is convenient, even if the batteries are not rechargeable. However, I wouldn't rely on these for security cameras. They're fine as a puppy monitor or critter cam, but they wouldn't be much help in identifying an intruder. With the 40% off the price was reasonable, but I wouldn't have been happy had I paid full price for these. There are less expensive cameras out there, but they are all either wired or much bulkier. However, at regular price, I would  probably have gone with one of them instead for our use, or if I needed better sound and image, gone with a more expensive brand, like Eufy, which also doesn't require a subscription.

Review: Have been wearing the Charge 5 for a month now. The App works seamlessly with my Apple phone. It has been enlightening and occasionally frightening. I was shocked to see how many times I wake up for 1 to 5 minutes per night without any recollection. How little “Deep Sleep” and “REM Sleep” I get per night. I’ve learned that those dreams that go on for hours can actually happen in 3 minutes just before I wake up in the morning. I’m 62 years old, retired, a widower with AFib and arthritis in nearly every joint. I can actually see my heart settle into a steady sinus rhythm as my meds kick in and start bouncing around again before my next dose 12 hours later. Same with the pain killers at night. I move very little until they begin to wear off, then my sleep becomes very restless and start flopping around like a fish. On bad nights I wake up 2-3 times an hour. My average resting heartbeats per minute is 60. On two nights while asleep last month the data showed sudden drops to 40 bpm for a few minutes. These are all things I would never known without this watch. Data that I can show my doctors and ask questions about. Is this serious? Should we change when I take my meds? Should we change meds? I’m still learning all the features of the watch and the App, in fact, I’ve just scratched the surface of all it can do. Highly recommend this amazing technology with one exception meant without sounding condescending. If you worry and consider making a doctors appointment every time you have a heart palpitation, wake up with a stiff shoulder or a slightly sore throat, all the data this watch traces may scare the heck out of you. Just my humble opinion.

For a device that auto-detects swimming and counts laps to fail when I'm really just floating around and not even pushing myself in the pool is a real disappointment. I used to love Fitbit, but after 10 years, with an app that only seems to get worse (especially the awful changes to the charts) I'm ready to move on.  Sorry, not sorry.  Fitbit left me.

Review: I had to change my initial review after using it in real world situations. When your barely moving to test the cameras they lead you to believe they will be a great option that’s easily installed and set up. But the ugly truth is that the detectable distance of the motion detection is the worst I’ve ever witnessed. As you can see in the pictures I’ve iploaded, the camera at the driveway doesn’t detect motion when people are at the fence door. You have to be 1-2 steps inside the yard for motion detection. I’ve moved the camera up and down in mounted height all while trying to keep out of people’s reach, adjusted sensitivity from minimal to maximum, tested day and night… it’s just terrible. The camera at the back door will not detect movement until you’re halfway from the steps in the picture to the camera location. This is completely unacceptable for any security camera regardless. Now, let’s top that off with even more bad news… because movement has to be so close to the camera before it detects motion, and the additional 1-2 seconds the camera takes to awaken and record causes the camera to barely catch the person on video and often times has nearly missed the person altogether. And… once again… the lack of distance for motion detection forces you to mount the camera at heights people can easily see, destroy, avoid, or steal. With a set up like this a burglar/thief can just do what they would do without a security system present because if you’re not watching live at the time you would miss everything… and especially your valuables. You would max out the 10 camera limit of the system just to monitor a very small location… trust me, I have 7 cameras to cover a 44x28 building and still have massive vulnerabilities. If the camera could just detect far enough out this system would be a really solid option but it can’t… so spend a little more and go with any other brand and thank me later.

With an SD card, you can have the cameras recording to it continuously, not just when it detects a motion.  There's been several times I've had to view an extra minute or two of an event, and this is not possible on the Blink cameras.  The most you get for a recorded event stored in their cloud is 30 seconds. I also discovered that the Ultra Hi Def audio that Amazon Music is pushing will only play with certain Amazon devices (and then you can't adjust the sound because your equalizer is stuck on flat settings) So, it seems that the more Amazon devices I buy, the more problems arise.  Part of this is just poor planning on Amazon's part and the unwillingness or inability to address issues.  Another part is that they are attempting to integrate too much into the Alexa app.  That app doesn't get many updates, so I've seen a large number of unresolved issues in the forums out there.  It was a mistake to get into all of these Amazon devices since they don't appear to have the support available to resolve issues.

Review: I was surprised by how little this thing can actually do and by how un-seamless the user experience is. The biggest smart-home items I have that I wanted to connect are my robot vacuum and robot mopper, from Neato and iRobot respectively.The Alexa app has robot vacuums as a main device category, but connecting them is really difficult. For the Neato vacuum, you have to connect your Neato account to Amazon. Fair enough, except that it only works if you used the same email address for both accounts! You will have to change your Neato email address to whatever you use with Amazon. Sorry if you wanted privacy.Connecting the iRobot mopper just didn't work. You have to install the iRobot skill, then add the bot as a device, but it won't connect to my Braava Jet robot at all. There is really no way to get help with it either. Amazon can't offer support for the dozens of 3rd party devices they claim to support, and iRobot doesn't know how to get it to work either. That is a hint of a failing ecosystem.I don't have any smart lights or anything like that yet, so what's left in terms of functionality is low-level features like the flash briefing. But even this seems like it's been neglected by Amazon. Many of the news sources on offer have stopped updating, so you can add them but Alexa just says they are unavailable every time. It's really difficult to customize also. I noticed if you ask Alexa how to edit your flash briefing she gives you inaccurate directions that don't reflect the current version of the Alexa app. If you manage to figure it out, you realize you can't really add useful things to your flash briefing like air quality for your city. It seems the boundaries of the experience are quite narrow, and they are becoming more narrow as the ecosystem shrinks. This is supposed to be a flagship device for Amazon and a key part of their strategy, but the experience has atrophied badly.

Review: Purchased Blink Indoor cameras, but replaced with these as Blink now requires a subscription.The good: Picture quality is good during the day, decent but a bit grainy at night. I have never had this issue with my EZ-Viz that has run for 3 years.  All adjustments require the app (no Windows client). The Alexa skill doesn't really seem to have a purpose, though perhaps it does something with an Echo Show.Overall the price is good and I have found nothing comparable for simple basic security, overlooking your driveway or backyard, or even in your home when away.  I've found TP-Link products in my experience to be well made and a good value. Review: I've had my original dot for some time now and have since added a few more as well as a show. Overall the dot has outstanding voice recognition, though it can be a little spotty if there's too much ambient noise....trying to tell alexa to turn down the volume when you have the music up a bit is pretty much an exercise in futility 😂. Sound quality is about that of a decent bluetooth speaker, fairly decent range and bass response you would get from a 2.1 soundbar. It's by no means a replacement for an actual home stereo system but having multiple dots in different rooms all linked together gives a nice encompassing feel.You have to be careful with alexa, she's worse than siri and will pop up when you even get close to invoking her name....and sometimes even when you aren't even close to it 🤷‍♂️, I don't know how many times I've had to tell her to shut up because she just decided to drop her two cents in. The voice recognition is so good that sometimes she can hear me from another room, though the farther away you are the more likely you'll have to either repeat yourself or cancel an action she thought she heard.Integration is pretty decent, the Amazon library being open to all to use and create skills in. I have most of my home's electronics integrated with alexa now, from the TV to my cameras and even my thermostat. If you're unsure if you're devices will be support simply download the alexa app and browse the skills section, the only skill I'm missing is for my Viper Smart Start, unfortunately I don't think Viper will ever create that skill.Setup and use are straightforward and not at all difficult. Have the app downloaded and opened, be on your home's Wi-Fi, and plug in your alexa. Hit add alexa device in the app and you'll be up and running in a few minutes. Getting everything set the way you like it and discovering new features.....I'm a few years in and still finding things.

Review: This is the first video system I have ever purchased.  At this price point I fully understood it would not be perfect compared to much more expensive systems.  After two weeks of use, here is what I think about the Blink system:GOOD:--Super easy to set up both cameras, base, and Wi-Fi.--Daytime clarity of the cameras is very good.--App controlling cameras and for viewing video is excellent and easy to use.NOT SO GOOD:--The clarity of the night vision video is terrible, but not surprising at this price point.--The motion detection is hit or miss -- sometimes misses people on my property or cars driving by.  I increased the motion sensitivity but then it started recording video constantly due to plants and trees moving due to heavy winds (I live in the desert -- lots of windstorms).--The system is somewhat laggy with my Wi-Fi.  If it picks up motion it does notify my phone there is motion, but it takes a few minutes to be able to view the video clip.  For me this is not a big deal -- but if you want the highest level of video security, it may be an issue.CONCLUSION:The Blink video system is a good value for the current price point.  It does provide decent video coverage around my property.  A few days ago it captured video of an intruder who stole some items from my garage.  The video was not clear, but I did get the alert to my phone and was able to call the police as a result (attached are vid caps).  I would say Blink is a very good choice for an entry level video system but if you are expecting the highest level of video security and coverage, this is not the right product.

Review: This camera was super easy to set-up with easy-to-follow instructions.  I currently have Blink cameras and bought this one to test/compare it vs Blink. The night vision, motion sensing, picture quality and sound are very comparable to Blink for about 1/2 the price. I also like that the large lithium battery is self-contained within the camera and can be recharged with supplied charging cord - saving the cost of lithium battery replacement.  After 3 weeks of outdoor Michigan winter use the battery was still displaying 75% charge - this was with a 15 second video record setting and approximately 10-15 video recordings daily.  Should be able to get 2 months or more of winter use between charges very easily. The camera is attached to the supplied mount by a bottom screw and is easily removed from the mount for charging. Also, like that they allow 3 days of free video storage before the videos are deleted. I review footage and delete as I receive notifications so I have not had the need to pay for the optional additional storage.  Camera is a little larger than a Blink camera but still light and relatively compact. The camera also has alarm settings audio/or blinking light, which can be enabled if wanted, which is a nice added feature.

Review: This is a decent and stylish fitness tracker, with a bold and very visible color display, and a nice flat design.  Design and display are much better than previous Charge models. As far as I can see, it tracks your daily steps pretty well. Unlike the older models, it no longer records steps climbed, which I miss. I like the fact that it is now water resistant. The sleep tracker is hit and miss, and there are nights where it has failed to record sleep, or recorded sleep when I've been awake. The heart rate monitor is good at lower levels, but falls far short at higher intensity workouts - luckily I have a heart-rate chest band for that.  When using the GPS function for a bike ride, you need to make sure it's fully charged in advance. Otherwise the battery lasts only a couple of hours, so the watch has switched off a few times on three hour rides recently. When it is recording your exercise, you can't (or I haven't found out how to) get back to the clock and see what time it is. Overall, I feel there is a certain illusion of accuracy about it, with lots of precise numbers that belie approximations in fact. But for a slim highly visible fitness tracker, it does the job

Review: This is the first speaker, not to mention Alexa device, I’ve owned, so I don’t have a lot of reference when I say it sounds great and works on voice command.  Alexa app is not perfectly intuitive.  I definitely had to do some troubleshooting to get Spotify to connect to the (now 4 total) Echo and Dot speakers in my house, as well as create groups of speakers, but was ultimately able to figure it out.  My partner finds talking like a robot is the best way to communicate to the Echo, but slow and clear seems to work fine for me (thank goodness).  Volume wise it’s pretty sensitive, so I can use a low tone a fair distance away and still be “heard” by Echo (which is both a little creepy and very convenient). We mostly use the Echo for music and controlling the Smart Plugs around the house.  “Drop in” and announcement features are amusing at best.  One thing that I don’t recall seeing in other Echo reviews that may be helpful to the un-Alexa-initiated, is that there are four set options for the word used to “wake up” your device: Alexa, Amazon, Computer, and Echo.  I don’t like using a person’s name for my device (I immediately turned off the chatty Alexa mode for simple bell chimes).  “Amazon” is like a ridiculous, unfunny joke of a word. And “computer,” while great for recreating starship Enterprise vibes, is just too much of a mouthful for regular, everyday use.  It’s a personal quirk for sure, but if it weren’t for the “Echo” option I would really question investing in more of these guys.

Review: We first bought 2 of these about a year ago and just recently bought 2 more. They're easy to use and easy to install. They have great pictire quality as well. The downside is the mounting piece only allows the camera to be rotated a very limited amount. For example we tried mounting ours along the roof line of our single story house but the mounting piece only allows the camera to move upwards so far, so the picture points about 45° down instead of outwards. We ended up moving the cameras down to the side of the house just above eye level which makes them super obvious and stupid looking but it's the only way we can get the camera to point out further. The other major downside, and this is the biggest for us, is the live view is delayed about 30 seconds. If someone comes to the door it's a good 20 seconds for the camera to alert us and then another 10-15 seconds to pull it up on our phones. By this time the person is long gone. Also, don't plan on speaking thru them. You can hear great from your app, however to speak to whoever is at your door you need to scream and even then the sound is extremely robotic and hard to understand. Overall for the price the quality is decent. They have worked well for us to keep an eye on our house while we are away and like I said, we did buy more of them. Just be advised if you are looking for the "talking" feature, these are not the cameras for you.

Review: Install and setup are a breeze, POE is the way to go! Support team is responsive and helpful. I would say that the motion detection is too sensitive or perhaps the AI needs some tweaking. I have it turned all the way down and it still picks up birds. Side note on that, it's fast enough to pick up and capture stills of humming birds, which is pretty impressive. It's way better to have it too sensitive than not sensitive enough and you can set the exact area that you want it to monitor. You can also black out areas that you don't want to record, which I think is a nice feature as I don't want to record my neighbors yard but I can still point the cameras in way that records all of mine. Night vision is excellent and the software is easy to use, most things are just point and click. As with all things network related you may have to play with your firewall settings a bit if you want to view the cameras remotely, but once I got that figured out the remote features are simple and work great. If you have a uverse firewall you'll need to enable DMZPlus for the NRV before you can connect remotely. Overall I'm happy with the purchase and will buy more from them as I expand the system.

I guess Amazon is removing all the hardware cost barriers so they can sell subscriptions to their HD/ULTRA Music service, which is where the real income is generated.My only criticism is that the Echo Studio can have a tad bit better audio quality. Review: Not a bad basic camera.  Overpriced for what it does.  Works to alert you when there is movement.  On medium sensitivity it will pick up a bird and send you an alert.  Will alert you when a moth flies by even at night.  Picks up people without a problem.  Does not provide you the option to Zoom in on a face or license plate so it has its limitations.  Would suggest that you use this as basic low level security camera but have a second system other than Blink to provide you with high resolution for person identification.  Because Blink will not be able to capture a face or license plate beyond 15 feet.  There is a delay of about 5 to 8 seconds before it will start recording a person walking in its field of view.  So you will miss capturing that much activity.Update, FIVE STARS on Blink Outdoor, my 5 camera set arrived on 12/11/2020 and installed it on 12/25/2020.  But by 2/27/2021, one camera went on the "blink."  It refused to operate and the app said "Off Line."  I removed it and found the batteries completely dead.  Replaced the batteries with fresh ones of Energizers-Ultimate-Lithium but in a few minutes the entire camera was warm to the touch.  I opened the rear cover and found the fresh batteries very hot to touch.  Then called Blink.  The gentleman was very knowledgeable and understood the camera was defective and then informed me that a replacement would be shipped and to expect it to arrive in 3 to 5 days.  I am so impressed with this company.  No hassles, just great service!  I highly recommend this camera and company.

Review: I finally bought this after the "black November" price break. I've been happily using a Charge 2 for multiple years, but it was down to 2 days battery and the screen had 2 cracks, which seemed to be lengthening. I was glad the Charge 5 price dropped. It's a good upgrade with more bells and whistles, but also comes with some annoyances. Others have mentioned these, so I'm not alone in having mixed feelings. So, it has a lot of new desirable functions, such as heart rate variability, ECG and SpO2. But unless you maintain the Premium Membership after the free 6 month trial, you lose them. Second, they dropped the "Stairs" measure. Though I didn't pay much attention to that in the last year, I did set goals for that in previous years; I don't know why they dropped it. Third, I can't find a "clock face" that shows my count up to hourly steps and total steps at once. That was on my Charge 2 always upon twisting  my wrist. Now, I have to tap and swipe the Charge 5 multiple times to see this. That's really annoying. Frankly, a lot of the "clock faces" don't make sense to me and the descriptions aren't very descriptive. I wish there was a simple way to design a display that shows Date, Time, Total daily steps and "hourly steps plus hours goal was achieved". That was my Charge 2 default screen.To Google/Fitbit: I just want you to know that I won't pay for Premium after the 6 month trial. I won't  use half the Premium features, so it doesn't make sense for such a high monthly and/or annual subscription.

Review: I am not sure if people reviewing these have never used a functional security camera or they just got a better product than me.  But I have four Blink cams.  Two outdoor, and two indoor.  The outdoor are somewhat useful, for things like seeing the delivery drivers and probably depending on angle could catch an intruder.  But as noted in MANY reviews, the fact that it only catches a maximum of 30 seconds is completely not useful for almost anything, and the live steam doesn't stay live unless you push the continue button.  So for me, trying to see my cat's activities or even for many deliveries, it really isn't useful.  I have fioptic internet w/ extremely high speed router, it's not my network.  Most of the outdoor activity is "OK" but there is definitely a lag with live views, and I have had it completely fail to catch motion as well (a delivery was made, but there is no video of it).  It's set on high sensitivity, but that doesn't seem to matter.  The indoor is almost useless, because of the 30 second limitation, I can't really monitor much.  I wanted to be able to check on my cat's eating and the pet sitter, etc, but it 1) doesn't catch it at the beginning and 2) doesn't have a long enough clip.  It's just pretty much wasted money for the inside ones.  The outside I think are probably somewhat useful, but I would not be at all surprised if I had something happened and Blink either missed it entirely or just caught the end of it.  And, it can only apparently record one camera at a time, so if something is happening in back and front of house, I'm out of luck.  Overall just a disappointment.  Will be replacing soon.  I've used the YI cameras and they are much better at recording and catching things from start to finish, but they have other drawbacks.  My simplisafe cam at my business is great, but they aren't cheap, but I may just switch to those at home as well.

Review: Overall, I’m not happy with Blink cameras and would not purchase them again. Let me explain: my expectations are high as a result of using Ring cameras. My biggest complaint is the motion detection—it’s terrible. It misses legitimate motion and conversely falsely activates frequently. Using the “Zones” feature (which is in Beta) is terrible too. This behavior is observed across multiple cameras. The capture delay is high. For example, as a person walks into and out of the view of the camera, much of the recording the of person approaching the camera is missed due to the delayed activation (and likely no buffered capture). The retrigger time cannot be set below 10 seconds, so you are likely to miss activity depending on how long your capture time is set to.The cameras are slow to respond—for example, if you are trying to speak through the camera, it takes a while to activate. It takes too long to activate live view between cameras because it’s as if though the Sync Module has to complete communications with one camera before interacting with another. Example, if you have multiple cameras and you are trying to follow motion from one camera to the next, this is very difficult.Overall, unhappy with Blink and would not recommend them.Here’s what’s good about the cameras, 1) battery life is amazing 2) good video quality 3) easy mounting, 4) easy setup, 5) they look nice) 6) appear to withstand rain without issue 7) attractive price when on sale.

Review: After nearly two years of owning this camera, we're ready to throw in the towel. The whole point of a security camera is that it's supposed to work on those rare instances when you need it to. It's very hard to get the motion sensitivity to the right level and it goes off constantly at the slightest movement, even after tweaking the zones to practically two feet away from the camera, which is of course useless from a security point of view.The worst is accessing Live View: it's maddeningly inconsistent and frustratingly out-of-order precisely when you need it most (i.e. when motion has been detected and you're trying to see what's up: who's at your door or on your property). The error message "Having trouble accessing Live View" is all too common, and if you try to click "More Info" you're directed to a useless support page that shows nothing about how to address or troubleshoot the problem. It's definitely not our wifi or battery life (we have the solar battery panel too) or connectivity issues on our end, as sometimes it works fine but more often than not it doesn't. Calling customer service is a joke and wastes endless time, with no resolution—probably because the simple plain fact is that this product just doesn't work well. This camera is not worth the money or trouble, nor does it reliably perform the functions a security camera should. Look elsewhere.

Review: If sitting in traffic listening to a jacked up stereo in the car next to you is what you like, this is the speaker for you: loud punchy bass with little fidelity or balance in the mid and upper range.  I like to test speakers with a range of recordings such as Hotel California by the Eagles, J.S. Bach's St. Mathew Passion, some Allison Krause, and a solo jazz guitar version of Autumn Leaves .  This failed on all counts particularly on the full orchestra and chorus of the Bach.  It seems like they took the original echo dot speaker, put a plastic fish bowl over it stuffed with loose fiber glass and called it a great speaker.  I don't think an audio engineer was anywhere near this project.  Voice alone is an interesting experience as well. Some annoying sympathetic harmonic resonances occur within the speaker for lower pitched male voices and are also there for the lower strings of the solo guitar.  Its not that I didn't want this to be a great speaker, I tried adjusting the bass, treble and mid range responses but nothing much changed.  This version of the echo speakers  is not one I would expect anyone will consider worth the price.  I returned it for a refund.

Review: The second generation plastic echo dots were great. Sound quality not so much if you were using it as a speaker, but the Alexa integration was awesome and the voice recognition was great. The third generation echo dot with the cloth covering still performed very well, but voice recognition not quite as accurate as the second generation. This fourth generation echo dot, the cloth covered sphere, would make a better baseball than voice assistant device. The integration with Alexa is obviously still great since that is what it is designed to do. However, this thing will not pick up voice if its life depended on it, which one day it just might. I can be in my bedroom about 5 feet away from this dot on the nightstand and it will not recognize the Alexa wake word. Interestingly enough, the second generation dot I have in the office diagonally across the hall and on the opposite side of the room, probably 35 feet away will pick it up fine. I will try to tell my bedroom echo to set an Alarm by saying "Alexa, set an alarm for 7AM", it will not respond at all, but I will hear from a distance, "setting an alarm for 7AM tomorrow", coming from the second generation dot in the office. Too bad these are outside the return period as I am currently looking at replacing the 4th gen with 3rd gen dots to see how that works, Otherwise I will be using these as baseballs and switching to Siri instead of Alexa and using Apple Home Pods in place of the echo dots. I would avoid these 4th gen dots and go with the 3rd gen if you are using it for any Alexa functionality.

Review: This camera/spot light was a bit pricey, so I was expecting a lot when I paid up to get it. Overall I'm quite happy with it, with a couple of minor quips. I bought the second battery, which was also a little pricey. I mounted it in a location that requires a ladder, so I wanted as much battery longevity as I could get. It's a bit difficult to explain but if you need to set up a motion zone that is not a perfect rectangle, this works fantastic. I also like the person only motion detection. This is great if you have pets roaming around the back yard. Ok now for the sorta bad. The area I have my camera mounted is fairly dark at night. The night vision is only so so. My gen 3 ring door bell is much better. When the spot light activates its better but I'm still a little disappointed. Occasionally I will get a false activation from motion outside the prescribed motion zone or even though I have person only mode on I will get a false activation from my pets. Review: The Arlo Essential Indoor Camera does not require an Arlo Smart monthly subscription—the product description is clear about that. But without one, you miss out on considerable functionality:  30-day cloud storage of captured video, emergency call services, detection zones within the camera’s field of view to name three. Basically, without a plan you can receive a push notification and email when motion is detected, can hear and see what is moving, and can sound an alarm if warranted. Those are some reasonable capabilities, but they are not at all unique nor are they competitively priced in this camera. There is also a significant delay in the live feed on top of the time necessary to notice the message/email and start the app. Without capturing video automatically when motion is detected and storing it for review later, there is little chance you’ll see anything besides the back of someone walking away with your TV. But if you are lucky enough to see something and want a picture, you’ll need to do a screen grab I suppose.But I also have an Arlo Base Station (VMB4000) that advertises seven rolling days of free cloud storage. I should be able to recover some functionality of the monthly plan by using the base station, right? Not so fast. Not only is there no way to automatically trigger a recording when there is motion using the base station, there is no way to do it manually either. Integration with the base station apparently gets you nothing; you still have no automatic or manual recording capability and can only get push notifications or emails.So, yes, this camera integrates with an Arlo Base Station, but why bother? To realize most of the camera's potential, you’re going to need to pay monthly.

Review: As someone who owns almost every product line for the last 20 years from Bose, this product was extremely disappointing. It makes zero sense for them to not make this compatible with SoundTouch. I installed the Bose Music app (required to do anything regarding settings for this device) and it was a huge inconvenience that tests the patience of any consumer. This is coming from someone who is rather tech savvy. Additionally, if you use this in an area that doesn’t have WiFi, you will not be able to change settings on this device at all. This was a deal breaker for me as my work center does not have WiFi (military base).I was willing to let that go until I realized that the sound quality is just not there. If you are in front of the speaker, you can’t get a good stereo image unless it’s able to reflect the sound back to you from a wall. Otherwise, you have no forward sound image produced by the speaker.The worst part about all of this was that there was an atrocious rattle coming from the right side of the speaker when playing any music with significant bass at about 35-40% volume. Anything above that would produce what can only be described as a farting rattle noice that was louder than the actual music itself. I did everything I could to see if it was something that could be corrected with bass and treble settings, however it could not be remedied. Upon further research, numerous consumers had this issue with Bose offering no fix besides resetting the device (this produces zero change in the rattling sound).Deeply disappointed in this device. Bose really needs to take the time to make their devices user friendly and intuitive enough to not limit settings for a device only for when you have WiFi. It’s a Bluetooth speaker too.

Review: I loved my Echo Dots, really.  I was gifted my first, purchased a second and then a third.  I brought the third, newest to my condo in Florida for the winter (as I had previously with my second).  So far, so good, no problems. Problems began. Started playing news and music back at my home in the north.  I know bc my spouse would call me to complain that the Echo Dots in Main House were playing as well as Sonos speakers.  Newest Echo Dot was not playing in Snowbird Condo even though command issued from it.  Re-booted, seemed to fix it for awhile.  Then problem migrated to Echo Dot 3 (brought south from Main House) and would not play NPR here.  It played it up north to disturb my spouse.  Spent a lot of time trouble-shooting, thought it was fixed.  And then it still would not play NPR station (from home town) in condo, only in Main House even though command issued from Snowbird Condo.  I tried to get rid of groups, etc. but this is getting absurd.  I fear disturbing my spouse up north, can't get the news down here and wasting a lot of time.  Some new software upgrades have made Alexa too smart for me and it looks like too smart for Alexa.  Since last sentence I spent more time dickering with settings within the app, rebooting (press the button unrelated to volume on top) to reconfigure.  By removing all labeling of rooms but getting it to prompt me for home locations, I finally got it to function here.  My spouse unplugged all devices up north but I suspect they will no longer play there.  It was not trivial to fix.  Then I'm old but I've worked with computers since 1968....

Review: My KALINCO  smartwatch in blackcolor comes with a charging cable, and user manual.  The wristband is quite soft.  It only needs a few minutes to set it up. All steps are quite  straightforward and are well documented in the user manual.It has all the features I need to help monitor my health. It provides all day multi-sport tracking. One amazing thing is it allows users to load pictures from photo to personalize the watch face.  I have been wearing the watch all day long, and feel very comfortable and secured.However there are two caveats: (1) after changing the  temperature format of the weather function on the app from  Celsuis  to Fahrenheit ,  the smart watch will display temperature in  F but  only for a few hours, then it will change back to Celsius again.  So you need to go to app to set it again. (2) the “Find Phone” function needs a second tap to  trigger the phone to ring if phone is found.  In other words, the first tab on the "Find Phone" will enable  the radar screen on the watch to spin,  with the second tap on the watch, the phone will ring if phone is found. Alexa integration is similar to other run of the mill integrations.  Nothing horrible. I'm kinda impressed that reviews don't call this out.  Unless you pay 3$ per month *per camera* they won't actually record anything. I gave up and paid for the subscription for my three cameras (sunk costs and all that), but that didn't fix anything beyond providing basic functionality. Review: It's taken me quite a while to get this smartwatch set up today.The user guide is very minimalist and, once you've downloaded the corresponding app (VeryFit), you are pretty well left to puzzle it all out on your own.I have just about got my head around the basics now though and, having explored a bit,  it is quite impressive.All the expected exercise monitors are here, plus some unexpected things like sleep and stress monitors.There are tons of different watch faces to choose from, admittedly most though are rather quirky and garish.The gesture to turn on function isn't as sensitive as a previous smartwatch I had, but is usable.Overall, once you've mastered the slightly clumsy interface,  it's not a bad budget smartwatch and should prove satisfactory if you want to monitor some basic fitness metrics without paying for an iWatch or Fitbit.**** Update ****I've spent literally hours trying to get Alexa set up on this watch, but without success.  I've logged into my Amazon account 20+ times and the app declares "Success! Your registration is now complete."  Alexa on the watch, however, doesn't work and keeps telling me to log into my Amazon account!This is rather disappointing and I was tempted to drop my rating to just 3 stars.  The other features are pretty impressive though (notably the detailed sleep data), so it remains at 4 stars.  I did use the link in "Help" to contact support about Alexa not working and await a reply.**** Update #2 ****No reply from tech support yet, but I've discovered what the problem was with Alexa.  The VeryFit app was attempting to connect to the American Amazon.com by default rather than Amazon.co.uk.  Once I had redirected the registration URL to the UK website (and changed Alexa's accent from American to English) all was working as expected on this smartwatch.  Wish they had added this information to the FAQ section of the app, as it took me hours of frustration before discovering the solution.

Review: I bought this last summer but wanted to wait until I went through a winter before giving them a review.Are they priced too high? It's kind of hard for me to criticize. On the one hand, the night vision needs some work and the two-way voice system needs to be improved but on the other hand you can remedy the night vision issues by installing some cheap motion lights and put them BELOW the camera a bit - you will get a nice color picture at night. If you require big time surveillance, then these are not for you (but are still effective) but most people don't need that - these cams made me realize I would have wasted my money if I purchased an elaborate wired system - there's no need for that unless you live in a high crime area.

Review: Alexa has become an integral part of our family, even if not the only or even the most used voice assistant. Anyway, I added the dot only because I wanted a cheap way to expand it to more rooms.At $50 it’s a great alternative, also because it adds features that non-Amazon devices currently don’t offer. One of those is the ability to control the Echo wall clock, not essential but a nice touch that only works with Echo devices.Setup is easy in a way that’s simply expected today. In this case, it involves a smartphone with the Alexa app. If this is not your first Alexa device, adding a second or third is very easy.The diminutive size may not have you expect great sound, and while audiophiles may snuff at it, the sound quality is great for voice and good for music. The bass is present but don’t expect it to rock your world.Microphone and subsequent voice recognition are good. PF course you get all Alexa functionality and a few that non Alexa devices don’t get. For instance, using a collection of Alexa speakers to announce dinner (all speakers broadcasting) works, but only if initiated from the echo. Non-Amazon devices on the same network are only recipients.Another issue is a fundamental one with Alexa. Unlike it’s colleagues from the other ecosystems, Alexa cannot think in 24hr format time. You can configure the displayed time on applicable devices, but the voice assistant simply cannot be configured to use anything other than the old fashioned AM/PM. Given the sophistication in many other areas, this is a weird omission.Overall, the speaker works great for my needs as a secondary device that can also control an Echo clock. Sound is good but will not be confused with a more potent device like the Belkin Soundstage.

If I forgot to activate exercise mode, it still showed accurate HR and would log zone minutes.  If it was in exercise mode, and I was having a break or forgot to turn off exercise mode, it also stayed accurate and would be able to display a low HR.  However since the last update everything seems to depend on exercise mode.  If I were to forget to turn on exercise mode and do any sort of exercise including intense sports like hockey, it barely registers any zone minutes and if I look at it the HR displayed is usually about half of reality.  On the other hand, now if exercise mode gets activated accidentally (or I forget to turn it off) I burn insane amounts of calories and zone minutes while doing nothing.  I've had this happen over and over.  One time it got turned on in my sleep and I somehow got 300 zone minutes while getting a nights sleep (mind you, I have no heart issues).  It's also happened while taking a nap on the couch.  Or just getting an extra 100 zone minutes while sitting on the couch for an hour after a workout.  I wish that exercise worked this way but it doesn't.  Why did Fitbit decide that the device needed to cheat via using exercise mode as the primary determination? Review: I bought this to replace my original Echo that was in the living room.  It is the main area where we listen to music in our house and I wanted something that could produce decent sound quality with range.  This is where the Echo Studio comes in and excels.  The rest of it's Alexa capabilities are just like any of the other Echos that I have used and works well. It's base has a non-slip material to it, so it does stay in place.  The activity ring on the top is not as visible when lit as the other Echo units, which is a bit of a double-edged sword. Review: There's a lot I like about the Tapo C100. In some ways it over-delivers - it isn't obvious from TP-Link's website that you can record and monitor the camera output from a PC using your own storage with no cloud subscription as well as to an internal SD card. Setup was a little messy and connecting to Netcam Studio (thanks to another reviewer for the hint!) took a small amount of head-scratching as I had to set up an account on the camera effectively. I also had mild palpitations setting the camera up as it spoke to me which I sure as h*** wasn't expecting. The picture was better than I expected, the mobile app on Android is good. As other have commented, the night vision looking through a window simply reflects the IR lights back but that's only to be expected. I haven't tried yet but I do expect to be able to view the camera stream on a Chromecast-attached TV.However, there's one irritation which, to my mind, reduces the usability of the camera. You cannot give the camera a static IP address so, when it upgrades firmware or you move it to another room or have a power cut, it can reappear with a different IP address. TP-Link suggest that you should be able to force your router to reissue the same IP address but this may not be possible for many routers and, frankly, the right way is just to let you chose a static address. It's lost a star for this and possibly future purchases as the irritation caused with one camera must surely be worse still with several. It's lost a star for this.I've been looking for a camera that allows easy recording to my own storage at a reasonable price. This is so nearly a perfect fit.

Review: We already had 5 Echo Dots when we decided to purchase a full-sized Echo to replace on of the Dots that had been hooked up to an external speaker. The Dot in our living room was connected to the external speakers to be used as the main music-player for the house, and while it worked very well, the setup took up a lot of our limited shelving space. We decided to get the Echo as a replacement after reading reviews when it was on sale for Black Friday, and are so glad we made the plunge. The sound quality and volume is so much better than the Dot/speakers, and does not take up any more room than the Dot by itself. We no longer have to worry about the volume of the Dot and the speaker system, as everything is now self-contained by the Echo.Setup was as simple as any of the other Echo products we've purchased, which is to say extremely easy. In fact, this Echo seemed to connect to our wifi even faster than the Dots would, and didn't encounter any errors while the old ones used to. Better yet, we have freed up a plug since we no longer have to plug in the speakers, and don't have to have the external speakers always powered on, so we're saving electricity.I love the look of the new Echo, with the white fabric case blending in well with our other white furniture. The ability to swap the case means we'll always be able to find something that matches if we ever get new furniture.The Echo has definitely convinced me that the Dot, while great for starting out, shouldn't be the end of the line for our smart speakers. I can see myself slowly replacing Dots with full Echos as we go.

Review: Blink is a camera we've all heard of dozens of times so I expected it to be a good camera and it's just ok. The picture/video from the camera is almost like a fish bowl lense filter is on it, motion detection is slow and the video has at the very least a 5 second delay. I tried to use this in a window to watch the deer that come to the feeder in the back yard but it didn't catch the motion through the window or maybe it's the distance. I also had to turn off all night vision for it as it would reflect back through the window and only give you a white light of a screen when trying to view night vision. Turned on a porch light and that seemed to work enough to see at night but it didn't pick up the motion. I now use it with the free trial to keep an eye on the dogs when they are home alone and out which is rare. I usually put them in the bedroom with a baby gate up so they can still see and hear what's going on inside the house so I don't even really use the camera. I'd send it back but it's not worth the cost of gas to drive to a drop off location at this point. Maybe I'll just give it to a family member who doesn't mind the delay, the poor night vision and the poor motion detection. Idt I'd trust it as a baby monitor or even to get live updates on pets bc of the delay. The audio is also very poor. The charging cable is very long. It actually came with a charging brick as well which my phone didn't even come with now a days and it is very small and could easily be concealed if it needed to be so I'll go half way and give 3 stars. Glad I learned my lesson with the cheap mini instead of buying the outdoor set first.

Review: I really like Echo products and Alexa in general but the speakers on this item are terrible, even with tuning in the Alexa app, and while it *can* connect to Bluetooth or AUX speakers, that's not ideal for a device that is (1) in my living room without room for another speaker, and (2) supposed to be a smart *speaker* itself. In my opinion, if a speaker doesn't sound good, don't buy. That's just me though, and yes, I know it was a cheap speaker so I'm not upset or anything. The main reason for my 3 stars is because Alexa's voice on this thing is so muffled I have to have the volume at 5 to hear her voice that sounds like she is wearing 25 masks so I can't use her at night because 5 is so loud that even just the sound of her muffling would wake everyone up. Also, placement is key as the microphones aren't that great. I have to be very loud when I call Alexa and pause for a few seconds after I say her name or she'll think I was talking to someone else and turn off, something Siri or Google Assistant don't do. I find myself asking her the same question 2 - 3 times before having her answer for this reason. It's an amazing device, don't get me wrong. Just not as convenient and "fit into your life" as Amazon makes it seem. This is most certainly a device that will drive non-techie people insane if they try to use. For this reason, I am the only one in my home who uses Alexa and everyone else strictly only uses the HomePods in our home because Siri is just easier to use, despite being arguably less knowledgable.

Review: Wristband:My main problem with the Charge 5 is that both of the wristbands provided don't stay attached to their connection to the watch face.  I'll just be walking around the grocery store, getting out of my car, or sitting at the dinner table and feel my watch fall of my arm because it will not stay attached.  I'm afraid to work out in the thing for fear of losing it on the trail!  I had a similar problem with the Charge 2, but it wasn't as bad.  This makes me think it's a design issue with FitBit and is really making me wary of buying another one.  The bands for the Charge 2 would also just break, but I haven't had the Charge 5 long enough to see how the band material holds up.Watch Interface:The interface on the Charge 5 feels clunkier than the Charge 2.  I feel like I have to scroll forever to just say I'm on a walk, and I have to do a couple taps to even see my steps.  The watch is bright and sleek looking, but it just doesn't seem super easy to use.
